legacy_observation_minimum.note: A bounded sample can detect a regression but is explicitly not a production SLO claim; limits.json records that distinction so a small sample is never quoted as an availability number.

legacy_routing_or_auth_failures.unit: new failures attributable to task traffic
legacy_routing_or_auth_failures.note: Zero. Coexistence on the existing queue is the premise of the whole rollout, so a new legacy failure is a stop rather than a budget to spend.

lambda_throttles.note: Zero: task submissions must not starve the shared ingress.

value.rule: whichever of percent or absolute is larger

legacy_p95_latency_increase.unit: percent or seconds, whichever is larger
legacy_p95_latency_increase.note: Fixed as a pair so a small absolute baseline cannot make a trivial slowdown look like a large regression, nor a large baseline hide a real one.

queue_age_recovery.note: Queue age must return to baseline within this window after task load stops.

task_spend_ceiling.note: Unknown spend is recorded as null, never zero, so a task with an ambiguous model handoff cannot appear free.

qualification_run_spend_ceiling.unit: USD for the whole qualification run
qualification_run_spend_ceiling.note: Separate from the engine development budget, so evaluation spend cannot be hidden inside it.

task_lifetime.note: Includes queue and input waits. Exceeding it is a visible deadline failure, never a silently abandoned task.

submit_body_bytes.note: Exercised by fixtures/invalid/submit-request-body-byte-limit.json, which materializes and measures a schema-valid request above 65536 UTF-8 bytes.

submit_instruction_characters.note: Exercised separately by fixtures/invalid/submit-request-body-too-large.json, which holds a real 16001-character instructions string.

progress_marker_visibility.unit: distinct authored markers within N seconds
progress_marker_visibility.note: Neither a heartbeat nor buffered final stdout satisfies this; limits.json states both exclusions explicitly, because either would let a silent task look observable.

stream_revocation.note: Bounded revocation is only meaningful because no presigned URL is ever issued; a presigned URL would outlive the grant that minted it.

stream_authorization_recheck.note: An open stream is re-authorized on this interval, not trusted for its lifetime.

cancel_observation.note: How quickly a healthy host must observe a durable cancel.

child_stop_confirmation.note: On expiry without a confirmed exit the outcome is cancellation_stop_unconfirmed with recovery required, not a clean cancellation.

host_heartbeat_interval.note: Past this bound execution health becomes unknown -- not unhealthy, and not healthy.

recovery_generations.unit: generations per task before any model send
recovery_generations.note: Exhaustion produces a visible failure or a visible recovery-required state; never a quiet abandonment or an invented exit.

recovery_publication_tries.note: All recovery bounds are themselves bounded by the task deadline.
